runner: ops/testing/journey-benchmark.sh, which stands the system up with the deployment drill (7 checks pass inside this run), seeds 1000 products, reindexes search, and drives ops/k6/shopper-journey.js through api-gateway from inside the cluster
why_this_exists: docs/evidence/load-benchmark-2026-09-09.json measures reads only. Until this run, no cart write, order write or outbox row had ever been produced under load, so nothing described write capacity or contention.
topology: one replica of each of the ten services in a scratch Kubernetes namespace on docker-desktop, with in-cluster PostgreSQL, Redis, Elasticsearch and Kafka, all single-node
traffic_shape: ops/k6/traffic-model.json, whose every parameter is assumed rather than observed: 1.2% of sessions complete checkout, 3.8% add to cart, think time 1-8s, 20 distinct shoppers each with their own token

run.artifacts: ops/k6/results/journey-20260909T214655Z/k6-output.txt (local only: ops/k6/results/*/ is gitignored, because every run writes a new timestamped directory of raw k6 output. The findings are in this file; rerun the benchmark to regenerate the raw log.)

reading: 1013 requests across 683 browses, 250 searches, 40 cart writes and 40 checkouts, with a 0% step failure rate and p95 226ms end to end. Every cart write that was attempted completed, and every cart that was filled checked out.
defects_this_run_found: The journey's session sampler, (VU * prime + ITER) % 1000, is deterministic but not uniform at these scales: with about fifty virtual users it visits only ~50 of 1000 residues and never fell below the 1.2% conversion threshold. 930 iterations produced zero checkouts while the run reported success -- a write benchmark that never wrote. Replaced with a hashed bucket, verified to reach the branch before being trusted.

Every cart write returned 403. The benchmark minted one token whose subject was 'load-shopper' while the journey acted as 'load-shopper-<n>', and CartController correctly refuses one user access to another's cart. The authorisation check was working; the load generator was wrong. Fixed by minting one token per synthetic shopper, which is also what real sessions look like.

k8s/seeds/job.yaml carried no Secrets at all, so seeding crash-looped on an unresolved INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN. This is the same defect fixed earlier in k8s/migrations/jobs.yaml; it survived because that fix was applied to the migration Jobs and the neighbouring file was never checked. Every kind: Job in the repository has now been audited.
limits: These numbers do not transfer to production: one laptop, one replica per service, a generated 1000-product catalog, and a traffic shape whose parameters are assumed.
8 journeys/second for 90 seconds is an exploratory point, not a saturation search. Nothing here establishes where the write path degrades.
The payment provider is the in-process mock, so checkout latency excludes a real processor round trip, which in production usually dominates it.
The outbox was not observed draining under load; that it drains after a broker outage is covered separately by ops/testing/chaos-drill-order.sh.
